item.title: Fewer people are moving to Copenhagen because of high housing prices
item.description: Since 2000, Copenhagen has gained 175,000 residents. The forecast shows the city is expected to grow by another 93,000 people by 2060, reaching a population of 765,000.

item.title: What internationals should know about neurodiversity, relocation, and life in Denmark
item.description: Relocation is also one of the most significant psychological stressors a person can experience. For neurodivergent individuals especially, moving country can quietly amplify challenges, write Kirsten Baldocchi and Sidsel Byskov Hansen

item.title: A space for women the government ignores
item.description: For International Women’s Day, we asked Rachel Sheary, Communications Officer and Journalist and author of The Danish Connection -a podcast also available on The Copenhagen Post -to write about international women in Denmark.

item.title: We asked Claus Meyer, co-founder of Noma, about food, restaurants, and internationals in Danish gastronomy
item.description: The renowned Danish food entrepreneur discusses Harlo & Meyer, Copenhagen’s competitive restaurant scene, and why international chefs have shaped Denmark’s gastronomy.

item.title: 155 Danes land in Copenhagen on special Dubai flight
item.description: A special flight with 155 Danes arrived at Copenhagen Airport Monday night from Dubai. Organized by the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the flight assisted those wishing to leave the Middle East following attacks by Israel and the US against Iran, which resulted in closed regional airspaces. item.title: DanChurchAid raises 12.5 million kroner for war zones
item.description: DanChurchAid collected 12.5 million DKK during Sunday’s annual nationwide collection. Around 12,000 volunteers participated, including Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen and other members of parliament. The funds will support work in war and disaster zones, specifically Gaza, Ukraine, and South Sudan, providing essentials like food, clean water, and blankets. item.title: Alex Vanopslagh slightly leads Troels Lund for PM
item.description: A recent Voxmeter poll for Ritzau shows limited support for Venstre leader Troels Lund Poulsen as Denmark’s next Prime Minister. Only 8.6% of respondents prefer him, placing him third behind Liberal Alliance leader Alex Vanopslagh (10.1%) and the incumbent, Mette Frederiksen, who leads with 29.9%. item.title: Analysis: Female bosses earn nearly 100k less than men
item.description: Djøf’s annual equal pay analysis reveals significant gender pay gaps in Denmark. In private companies, female managers earn an average of 98,000 DKK less annually than male counterparts, representing a 7.8% unexplained gap that cannot be attributed to education or seniority. For private employees without management responsibility, the unexplained gap is 6.4%. Public sector disparities […]
